business_problem: Financial Times needed to support a growing subscriber base and broader product portfolio without overwhelming its service teams, while more than half of incoming cases could potentially be handled through self-service. Manual workflows across email, phone, and web chat, fragmented tooling, inconsistent experiences across desktop, mobile, and app channels, and the need to scale support globally were limiting efficiency and service quality.
solution_summary: Infosys and its subsidiary Fluido redesigned Financial Times' customer-care operation around AI-assisted intake and case handling inside a consolidated service stack. Subscriber requests arriving through web, email, phone, and chat were redirected where possible to an AI-powered ChatBot with guided self-serve flows so common questions could be answered without agent intervention. For issues that still required human support, Web-to-Case shifted intake into a web-based workflow that reduced spam and standardized case submission, while Einstein for Service automated case classification to improve routing speed and consistency. LiveChat (MIAW) added asynchronous digital conversations across channels, and Twilio plus internal tools were unified with the Salesforce Einstein environment to simplify operations. The rollout also introduced user-verification steps for online submissions and generative reply recommendations, giving FT a more scalable, globally supportable service model.

data_flow: Subscriber issues enter from web, email, phone, and chat channels. The AI-powered ChatBot handles common requests through guided self-service, Web-to-Case captures remaining digital submissions, Einstein for Service classifies the cases, and LiveChat (MIAW), Twilio, and internal tools support asynchronous conversations and agent workflows until cases are resolved.
business_outcome: The pilot reduced deflectable case volume, shifted more work into digital channels, saved agent time through automated classification and generative reply recommendations, shortened resolution times for online submissions, improved cancellation saves, reduced ghost chats and spam, and helped FT deliver record customer-satisfaction scores while scaling support more efficiently.
metrics: 30% (50k) reduction in deflectable case volume (on track to deliver FY target 50%).

17.4% cancellation-save rate, up from 14% in 2024 as a result of agents having more time to focus on value-added cases
Highest ever CSAT scores; 92% ease of help, 97% effectiveness of service
